items.note: Brochure (PDF, 2 pp.) confirms: trial start 11 March 2022; closures Fressgasse from 11.3.22, Marktstrasse from 21.3.22, Kunststrasse from 4.4.22; short-term spaces on Kunststrasse and Fressgasse become 'Erlebnis- und Begegnungsraeume'; all garages reachable via the ring; 9,500 spaces in garages/underground car parks. Off: the draft places all three closures 'at Paradeplatz', but the brochure puts the Kunststrasse and Fressgasse closures at Paradeplatz and the Marktstrasse closure at E1/E2.
items.corrected_text: A traffic trial from 11 March 2022 blocked through-traffic on Fressgasse (from 11 March) and Kunststrasse (from 4 April) at Paradeplatz, and on Marktstrasse at E1/E2 (from 21 March), turning the short-term street parking spaces on Kunststrasse and Fressgasse into public space. The city said all garages stayed reachable from the ring road and gave about 9,500 spaces in garages and underground car parks.

items.note: Brochure map lists 30-minute tariffs: G1 1.00, H6 0.50, C1 1.00, C5/D5 0.50, D3 1.00, N1/N2 1.00, N6 1.00 (N7 CinemaxX 1.20). Text states the reduced first-half-hour tariff is cheaper than the short-term street spaces had been. All figures match.

Page title matches. Page says the trial was planned for one year from the start; dismantling in spring 2023 was staged (Kunststrasse, then the bicycle street, then Fressgasse); the Fressgasse closure was lifted on Friday 12 May 2023 at 12:00, completing the dismantling; bicycle parking, delivery zones and restaurant parklets on Fressgasse and Kunststrasse stay; on 13 June 2023 the Hauptausschuss asked the administration to draw up a traffic and design concept aiming to reduce car traffic on Fressgasse and Kunststrasse. This is a mandate to draft a concept, not a decision on measures; the text describes it correctly.

The bylaw was adopted by the council on 31.05.2022 and took effect 01.01.2023. Annual fees: 63.75 (2023), 95.63 (2024), 127.50 from 01.01.2025. The hardship clause (SGB II recipients) sets lower rates of 51.00/76.50/102.00.

Amended bylaw adopted 11.12.2025, in force 01.02.2026. Zone 1 costs 1.00 EUR per started 15 min and Zone 2 costs 0.50 EUR. Zone 1 covers the area inside the city ring, the ring itself, the palace and main-station areas and western parts of Schwetzingerstadt/Oststadt. 4 EUR/h is simple arithmetic. The bylaw does not give the previous rate, so it does not show a price rise.

Amtsblatt 16 April 2026, p.3 'Innenstadt: Erste halbe Stunde Parken jetzt kostenlos': 13 MPB garages, underground car parks and lots in the Quadrate, at the Wasserturm and the Collini-Center; almost 4,000 spaces; first 30 min free; 2 EUR for the first hour; 4 EUR/h at street meters in the centre; 1 EUR/h from 21:00 at the latest; 3 EUR flat for the whole night until 6:00. The PDF's own title is 'Amtsblatt KW 16 barrierefrei'.

MPB release dated Mannheim 18.07.2024 (URL 2024/07/19; the page title is in German even at the /en/ URL). MPB acquires the N7 garage from the Heinrich Vetter Foundation as of 01.08.2024 and the purchase agreement was signed. The garage has 363 spaces and is still known as the Kaufhof garage 'for the now demolished department store'. MPB plans a mid seven-figure investment over the next four years in digital parking technology and renovation.

Heritage justification (Landesamt fuer Denkmalpflege, 'Stand 11.12.2024') says N 2 is a cultural monument under s.2 DSchG BW. It was built 1964-1967 'mit ... 505 Stellplaetzen'. The claim that MPB later called N2 one of the city's young listed buildings is not in this document (nor in the MPB plate-recognition page). The PDF has no title metadata; the draft title mixes the file name with a description.
items.corrected_text: The state heritage office's justification, dated 11 December 2024, classes the N2 multi-storey garage (built 1964-1967 with 505 spaces) as a cultural monument.
items.corrected_title: Liste der Kulturdenkmale in Baden-Wuerttemberg, Teil A1: Begruendung der Denkmaleigenschaft - Parkhaus N 2 (Landesamt fuer Denkmalpflege)

items.note: Page dated 20.10.2025 says the plate is captured at entry and entered at the pay machine, so the paper ticket is dropped. The long-term aim is to equip all sites. Sites listed: C1, D5 (TG), G1 (TG), Hauptbahnhof P1-P4, Klinikum TG and Klinikum P3, U2 (TG), Messe P6-8 and Messe Grossparkplatz P20. All match the draft.

Press release 15.03.2023: there were previously four charging spaces, now six each on levels 1 and 3 (twelve 22 kW wallboxes). Operator is B+B Parkhaus with MVV as back-end partner. It is the largest offer of any underground garage in the Quadrate, and B+B recently introduced ticketless parking. 'Privately run' is not stated outright, but the release names B+B Parkhaus as operator. The release has no separate title beyond its headline, which matches.

heidelberg24 page (title matches the HTML title; update of 26 Oct 2020). The N7 Kaufhof store has been closed since 15 October (originally due 17 October) 'nach immerhin ueber 40 Jahren'. Diringer & Scheidel signed the purchase contract on Friday 23 October. The page also calls N7 one of the stores set to close for good.

Rheinpfalz 07.06.2024: 16 of 92 stores were originally to close on 31 August under the insolvency plan. Six, including Mannheim, were saved, based on later offers from landlords (the insolvency administrator's statement). In Mannheim the new owners of the property at Paradeplatz presented their plans. Title matches.

Rheinpfalz (12.07.2023): BUGA runs 14 April to 8 October at Spinelli-Park and Luisenpark. Car visitors should use P20 at the Maimarkt, 8.50 EUR/day online (9.50 at the lot). A P+R shuttle bus runs, and special tram lines (BUGA-Express BS, BL) run from the main station. Title matches.

Wochenblatt-Reporter (17.10.2023): more than 2.2 million visitors by the last day of the 178-day event at Spinelli and Luisenpark, against 2.1 million calculated. According to the visitor survey, many guests also visited the city centre. Title matches. The survey is presented in the BUGA managing director's review; 'organisers' survey' is a fair reading.

FashionUnited (4 March 2025): a deadly car ramming ('Todesfahrt') on Rosenmontag (3 March 2025) killed two people in the city centre. Galeria at Paradeplatz and Peek & Cloppenburg on the Planken did not open on Tuesday. Engelhorn closed from the afternoon and reopened on Wednesday. The '3 March' date comes from Rosenmontag 2025, not printed on the page.

Amtsblatt 10 July 2025 p.3: the council adopted the Masterplan Mobilitaet 2035+ as a traffic framework plan on 1 July. It has over 100 measures (36 key measures) incl. public transport, cycling and quality of public space. The administration is tasked to seek state certification as a Klimamobilitaetsplan. Implementation depends on available budget, and the council keeps approval of individual measures. Note: the PDF metadata title reads 'Amtsblatt KW 01 barrierefrei' (a stale template); the draft title follows the document header, which is correct.

corrected_summary: Mannheim ran a one-year traffic trial from March 2022 that blocked through-traffic on Fressgasse, Kunststrasse and Marktstrasse and turned short-term street parking into public space; it was dismantled by 12 May 2023, after which the council's main committee asked for a new traffic and design concept, and the council adopted the Masterplan Mobilitaet 2035+ as a framework plan in July 2025. Resident permit fees rose in steps to 127.50 EUR a year from 2025, on-street parking in zone 1 has cost 1 EUR per 15 minutes since February 2026, and in April 2026 the municipal operator MPB made the first half hour free in 13 city-centre facilities; MPB also bought the 363-space N7 garage in 2024 and has converted a number of sites to ticketless number-plate entry. Other dated events include the closure of the Kaufhof store in N7 in October 2020, the 2023 Bundesgartenschau, the June 2024 reprieve of the Galeria store at Paradeplatz, and store closures after the March 2025 car ramming in the city centre.
